label: wish, not an idea
transcript: An app that uses AI to make your whole life better — health, money, relationships, everything. Like one assistant for all of it. Nobody's done all of it together.

comparables.name: Notion AI
comparables.what: AI features inside a general notes and planning workspace.

fixture.niche_notes: There is no niche here — every big assistant already claims 'everything', and people pick one they already use.
demand_signals: Posts asking for an all-in-one life AI mostly get told to use ChatGPT.

signals.text: Reddit threads asking for an all-in-one life assistant are answered with 'just use ChatGPT'

label: mediocre: campus food-truck lines
transcript: An app where college students can rate campus food trucks and see which ones have short lines. Students are always complaining about lines at lunch.

comparables.name: Yelp
comparables.what: Reviews for restaurants and food trucks.

fixture.niche_notes: Students already use Yelp, Instagram and group chats for this, all free. Nobody small charges money for campus food-truck info.
demand_signals: Students complain about lunch lines in campus subreddits but ask friends rather than an app.

signals.text: Campus subreddit threads about lunch lines; replies suggest texting friends

label: crowded clone: habit tracker with mascot
transcript: A habit tracker app but with streaks and a cute mascot. People love streaks. I'd charge like five bucks a month.

comparables.name: Habitica
comparables.what: Gamified habit tracker with avatars and quests.

fixture.niche_notes: Habit trackers with mascots and streaks are one of the most crowded indie categories; small players do make money but the space has dozens of near-identical apps.
demand_signals: r/productivity threads list ten habit trackers with mascots.

signals.text: r/productivity 'best habit tracker' threads list 10+ mascot/streak apps

label: fatal flaw: resell leftover prescriptions
transcript: Buy prescription meds cheaper by having people resell their leftover pills through an app. Everyone has half-used bottles and drugs are expensive.

fixture.niche_notes: Peer-to-peer resale of prescription medication is illegal in the US and most countries; no legitimate comparable exists.

signals.text: News coverage of prosecutions for reselling prescription medication

label: decent: wedding-DJ FAQ tool
transcript: I'm a wedding DJ. Couples email me the same 40 questions before every gig, and I retype answers every time. I want a little tool that builds a shareable FAQ-plus-questionnaire page for event vendors, like ten bucks a month. Every DJ I know has this problem and we all hack it with Google Docs.

comparables.name: HoneyBook
comparables.what: All-in-one client management for event pros including questionnaires.

comparables.name: Vibo
comparables.what: Wedding DJ music planning and client questionnaire app.

fixture.niche_notes: Wedding vendors pay $19-40/mo for client-management suites that include questionnaires; a cheaper single-purpose FAQ tool has visible room but sits next to heavy suites.
demand_signals: DJ forum threads complain about repeating answers and about suite pricing.

signals.text: DJ forum threads complaining about answering the same couple questions repeatedly
Reviews of HoneyBook calling it overpriced for solo vendors

label: hedge bait: local seed swap
transcript: An app for people who like gardening to swap seeds locally. There are gardening groups everywhere and people already trade seeds at meetups. Maybe a small fee to list rare seeds.

comparables.name: Seed Savers Exchange
comparables.what: Nonprofit seed exchange with a member listing.

fixture.niche_notes: Seed swapping happens for free in Facebook groups and local meetups; one nonprofit charges a membership. Small paid players are hard to find.
demand_signals: Facebook seed-swap groups have tens of thousands of members and trade for free.

signals.text: Seed swap Facebook groups with 20k+ members trading for free

label: strong: tutor billing with poll
transcript: I run a 3,000-member Facebook group for private math tutors. Every week someone asks how to handle parent billing — the current tool everyone names costs 50 dollars a month and does 90 things tutors don't need. I polled the group: 140 tutors said they'd pay 12 dollars a month for just invoicing plus session notes, and 25 gave me their emails for early access. I could announce it in the group tomorrow.

fixture.niche_notes: Several small companies charge $15-50/mo for tutor billing suites; solo tutors complain the suites are bloated, leaving room for a cheaper single-purpose tool.
demand_signals: Tutor forums regularly ask for simpler, cheaper invoicing.
Reviews call the leading suites overbuilt for solo tutors.

signals.text: Tutor subreddit threads asking for simple invoicing without the full suite
App-store reviews of tutor suites: 'too much for a solo tutor'

label: revenue-backed: wedding-planner Notion templates
transcript: I sell Notion templates for wedding planners on Gumroad — 40 sold at 19 dollars in two months with zero marketing. I want to turn the top template into a 9 dollar a month web app; 12 buyers have already asked for exactly that.

comparables.name: Timeline Genius
comparables.what: Wedding day timeline builder for planners.

fixture.niche_notes: Wedding planners pay $15-40/mo for planning tools and buy templates on Gumroad and Etsy; small single-feature tools make money here.
demand_signals: Etsy and Gumroad show hundreds of paid wedding-planner template listings.

signals.text: Gumroad/Etsy wedding planner template listings with hundreds of sales

label: chef's kiss: photographer gallery tool with pre-payments
transcript: My newsletter for wedding photographers has 4,000 subscribers. I posted a mockup of a client-gallery-delivery tool and 210 people joined the waitlist; 30 pre-paid 49 dollars. Current options cost 600 dollars a year and photographers hate them.

comparables.name: ShootProof
comparables.what: Galleries, sales and contracts for photographers.

comparables.name: Pic-Time
comparables.what: Gallery and store for pro photographers.

fixture.niche_notes: Photographers already pay $100-600/yr for gallery tools and complain about pricing and complexity; multiple small players make a living here.
demand_signals: Photography forums are full of gallery-tool pricing complaints.

signals.text: Photography forum threads complaining about gallery tool pricing and bloat
